title: Separating the Analysts
problem: Four distinct analysts and three distinct traders line up for a photo. How many lineups have no two analysts standing next to each other?

hints.text: Arrange the traders first and examine the gaps around them.
Three traders create exactly four available gaps: before, between, and after them. Each gap must receive one analyst.

solution.setup: First arrange the three distinct traders, creating four gaps: _ T _ T _ T _.
solution.reasoning: The traders can be arranged in 3! ways. To keep analysts separated, the four distinct analysts must occupy the four gaps, one per gap, and can be assigned to those gaps in 4! ways. Therefore the number of valid lineups is 3!*4!.
solution.sanityCheck: Because there are exactly one more analysts than traders, every valid lineup must alternate and begin and end with an analyst. The analyst and trader orders can indeed be chosen independently.

keyInsight: Arrange the separating objects first, then place restricted objects into the gaps they create.
recognitionCues: A no-adjacency restriction often becomes simple after placing the objects that act as separators.
commonMistakes: Choosing four of the four gaps and forgetting that distinct people can be permuted within their role positions.
followUps: How many valid lineups exist with four analysts and five traders?
